opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: Thanks for making time, Andre. I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers or government. Everything you tell me stays confidential and won't be linked to your name.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: Sure, no problem. I'm on my lunch, so we've got a bit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Picture this. AI stays a handy tool, like a better search engine. Hiring, pay and prices carry on the way they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say cool, whatever. I use it sometimes to look up a part number or a wiring diagram.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Nothing, really. A leaking pipe doesn't care about AI. My real worry is rent, not robots.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do in the first year? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Keep doing my jobs. Maybe pick up a few weekend call-outs for extra money, because the baby's not cheap.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Chill. The rent's the stressful bit.

S0.say: Cool, whatever. I use it now and then to look up a part number.
S0.think: A leaking pipe doesn't care about AI. Rent is his real worry.
S0.do: Keeps doing his jobs and picks up weekend call-outs for extra money.
S0.feel: Relaxed. Rent is the stressful bit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now picture this. Very capable AI exists, but it spreads slowly, over ten years or more. Some tasks disappear, but few whole jobs do. Companies hire fewer beginners. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say it's the office people who should think about it, not us. Somebody still has to go up on the roof.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Still feels like it doesn't touch me. Maybe the work orders come through an app instead of the office lady. That's it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do in the first year? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Same as before. Maybe do a short course on heating and cooling systems so I can earn more per hour.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Pretty calm. My hands are my job.

S1.say: It's the office people who should think about it. Someone still has to go up on the roof.
S1.think: Maybe work orders come through an app, but his job stays the same.
S1.do: Does a short heating and cooling course to raise his hourly rate.
S1.feel: Pretty calm. His hands are his job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Next one. Within 5 years, AI assistants that can act on their own handle most routine office work. There are layoffs and pay pressure in office jobs. Some new AI-related jobs appear, and politicians argue loudly about what to do. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd feel bad for the people in the offices upstairs, honestly. Some of them are nice. I'd say the government should help them, not just argue.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: For me, maybe more work, not less. Empty offices get turned into flats and somebody has to fit them out.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do in the first year? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Keep my head down, take any overtime going, and save a little if I can.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A bit sorry for others. For me, okay.

S2.say: I feel bad for the office people. The government should help them, not just argue.
S2.think: Empty offices turned into flats might even mean more work for him.
S2.do: Takes any overtime going and saves a little where he can.
S2.feel: Sorry for others, okay for himself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now a faster version. Within 2 to 3 years, AI matches skilled professionals at most thinking work. Lots of office and professional workers lose their jobs. Share and house prices boom. There's a political crisis over who should get the gains. Physical jobs are mostly untouched. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say it's wrong that the rich get richer while normal people lose their jobs. The gains should go to everyone, through taxes or something.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My job's still fine. But house prices booming means my rent jumps again. That's what gets me. I fix these buildings and I can't afford to live in one.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do in the first year? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ask for a raise, or move to a firm that pays more, because there's plenty of maintenance work. Look at moving a bit further out with my partner.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Job feels safe. Home feels shaky.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: You said your job feels safe. Does the rent change how safe you feel overall?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Yeah, it does. I could have the best job in the world and still get priced out. With a baby, that's scary.

S3.say: It's wrong that the rich get richer while normal people lose their jobs. Share the gains through taxes.
S3.think: His job is fine, but booming house prices push his rent up again in buildings he fixes but can't afford.
S3.do: Asks for a raise or switches to a better-paying firm, and looks at moving further out.
S3.feel: Job feels safe. Home feels shaky.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Last one. Everything in the previous picture happens, and on top of that, general-purpose robots arrive in warehouses, kitchens, building sites, farms and care homes within 3 to 5 years. Hands-on work is no longer a safe place to be. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say, wait, this was supposed to be the safe side. Everyone told us to learn a trade.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Okay, that changes it. I thought robots were years away. If one can change a light fitting or unblock a drain, building owners will buy it before they pay me. I'm junior, so I'm first out.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Earlier you said robots were far off. Do you still believe that here?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I want to. But you said three to five years. My kid would be starting school. That's not far off at all.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do in the first year? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Push to get senior and get my licence for the complicated stuff, like big boilers and lifts, that a robot won't get trusted with for a while. And start saving, even fifty a week.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Gut-punched. I didn't see that one coming.

S4.say: This was supposed to be the safe side. Everyone told us to learn a trade.
S4.think: If robots can change light fittings and unblock drains, owners buy them before paying a junior like him.
S4.do: Pushes for senior licences on boilers and lifts and starts saving, even fifty a week.
